slug: 2026-04-07 São Tomé and Príncipe Launches Citizen Portal

facts.fact: CDPI says the Government of São Tomé and Príncipe launched its Citizen Portal on 27 March 2026, in beta, supporting tax certificates and police clearance certificates.

systems.owner: Government of São Tomé and Príncipe

facts.fact: RSTP reports INIC presented the beta version of the Portal do Cidadão at its 18th anniversary ceremony, with the Prime Minister calling it the launch of the portal.
India's MEA brief says the National Citizen Portal (gov.st), enabling access to public services through National ID-based login, was launched on 27 March 2026.

systems.owner: Government of São Tomé and Príncipe

note: Document reports only prototype demonstrations and a planned portal launch, no service launched or piloted.
The document names the national data centre only as sea-level and at flood risk; it does not say it rents to others, who owns it, or any service or backup site.
Document states nothing on government services online.
The 150+ services portal is described as delivered by Phase 1 and as expected outcomes; the page does not say a service is live or piloted.

facts.fact: São Tomé and Príncipe's foreign ministry launched a Document Issuance System at its embassy in Portugal, letting the diaspora request birth certificates, the national identity card, criminal record certificates and certificates of legal capacity to marry through a digital portal of the Directorate-General for Registry and Notary.
Sao Tome and Principe launched the beta version of the Portal Unico do Cidadao at INIC's 18th anniversary, announced by the government.

systems.system: Tribunal de Contas electronic accounts system

note: Planned 2027 filing system for audited entities, not delivered, and not a service for citizens or business.
Platforms for internal records and diplomatic and service passports; no citizen or business service stated, and the Citizen Portal is still to be created.
The record answers no; a database's no is not a fact.
A police and telecom operator protocol aims to create digital public-security services; none is said to be launched.
